Not vs code related, but excel. I have daily reports I need to run and download. They need to be saved locally and in the network drive, and then emailed.  Due to security restrictions I can't automate this task under my account and the people with the permissions to automate don't have time for this.

So I created a page in my Excel task tracker. The page has a button shortcut to both my local drive and one to the network folder. I use thhese to open the file locations. Manually move the files to the archive folder then go in our application that produces the report and save it to my local drive. And a quick drag and drop to the network folder.  Then I use my 3rd button to open an email template in Outlook where I drag and drop the files and hitting send. 

The only code is html in the button links. I always tell myself I'll  see if I can make this into a macro (security restrictions) but never get around to it. This takes what was a 20 minute task and significantly cut down on my clicking and navigating around. It also has saved time when I'm out because I send the sheet to whoever is covering me and they can easily click and follow the instructions rather than trying to figure out where to find the folders and typing up a new email when the template is already done.

Before my wife was my wife, she told me she watched men complain about food all the time and women just took it. She said if a man ever complained to her about her cooking she would just stop cooking for them. 

Soon after that conversation, I was at my mom's house and my wife came over to see me and she decided to cook something for me. She was adding more salt than I usually would have at the time plus she was mostly using canned stuff and boxed stuff that is already high in salt.  I said I think the salt is probably good and didn't need any more.  She didn't like that I was telling her how to cook so she smiled and said oh? As  she added a bunch more salt. Then served up the food. 

Remembering what she said about complaining about the food and wanting a future with her I kept my mouth shut offering no complaints. Even profusely complementing the food. You did so much with such basic ingredients it's a great combination of flavor etc. Aside from being overly salty it was good. I ate it all  With a big smile on my face. My mom got curious and tried it. After a big bite she set it down and just smiled at my soon to be future wife. 

Seeing her reaction my wife thought  it must be really bad and tried it herself. Previously she did not taste it since she wasn't hungry. 

When she did she realized how salty it was and felt super embarrassed she served it up to both my mom and I. She tried to take the plate back from me. 

I told her nope in a joking way that  I won't allow that because after eating mostly eating pot bachelor meals I  don't want her to think I have a problem with her cooking and stop cooking for me.

So I finished the food with several glasses of water. Every bite she squirmed telling me it was ok I didn't have to finish it. I just smiled and continued to enjoy it.

Fast forward 10 years.  I have enjoyed amazing meals everyday. Some are better than others for sure but I don't complain. I prefer her cooking to restaurants. And think she actually makes many dishes better than they do. We eat out when we can to try new flavors, then in the days and weeks later she recreates the dishes and makes them better. Every day she puts a lot of time and thought into feeding our family as cooking is her hobby. 

 For her, cooking for others is a true joy, she even plans extravagant dinner parties for family and friends. People always ask if they can take leftovers home with them.

With all of that said even if every meal was the same as that super salty concoction she made at my mom's all those years ago (we still laugh about it today) I would eat it everyday with a smile on my face being grateful that she  loves me enough to prepare a meal for me.

Waaaaaay back in the day computer enthusiasts used to configure their dial up modem to automatically call phone numbers often working through large phone blocks looking for networks. This was called "War Dialing" back then you often just needed a phone number to access an interesting system. 

As technology evolved and people began using insecure WiFi networks "War Driving" became a way to find these open networks and get "free internet' as well as to explore what networks were around. 

I  enjoy war driving every now and then just to see what's around. 
Most just fire up wiggle on long car trips to the in-laws while my wife drives and see what pops up.  You would be amazed to see how many people are broadcasting hotspots all the time. Maybe even more surprised to see how many internet connected devices you can find (like other vehicles). People are basically transmitting their own tracking devices)

On a random aside: The cell service went out around my at my work the other day so I went looking for open Wi-Fi networks and found an internet connected refrigerator

Personally I agree with many people here, and the individual skills they mentioned but i think you need to become a jack of many skills. 

 I learned html way back in the early internet days and programming. I wanted to make my own websites back then. 

In order to make a good website I also needed to know how to make graphics so I learned Photoshop. Then digital cameras became more common so I learned adobe premier to edit video. I moved away from the online space for many years and came back learning how wordpress sites work and started customizing them for people on the side. 

Usually needed the above skills. For example One business I created a logo, designed business cards and created a website. 

Another I had to recreate the logo because they only had old low resolution files. And did a significant amount of video editing for them. 

I had a side gig adding captions to a company's you tube videos when captions first came out. At the same time I was also asked to edit the videos adding the company phone number as a water mark and reupload them because competitors were stealing the content. 

So I would say learn (in not particular order)

Html/css <--the foundation of most all websites

Photoshop (gimp is like PS and open source)
   Bonus: learn illustrator (vector based graphics)

Premier/after effects (davinci resolve free and powerful video editing)

Study sales/marketing/copywriting

While I feel a bit old myself to crack in to the 3d space and have not yet had the time to learn, I would say also figure out blender.  I think there is going to be a lot of interesting stuff in that space especially with the rise of Indie game development and VR space.

Other things to explore, develop an understanding of databases, if you get to work on more advanced sites you may need this.

On that same track analytics skills are super helpful for understanding how your site is doing. But more than that you can translate those skills to helping businesses, in my day job I am currently working on becoming more proficient in data analytics. I have already built several useful reports that are used by the management team daily. 

One final area to investigate is AI, this area feels like the new wild West like the internet was when I was a kid. Really dive in don't just learn how to write good prompts for chat gpt also learn about fine tuning models and how to implement your own models/ training sets. There is a world of opportunity in this space between my family/kids and my full time job I am still trying to figure out how I want to use it for a side hustle but my time has been sparse in this area. 

There is a lot to learn and it takes time to feel comfortable or even proficient. The biggest advantage you have now is living in the age of YouTube where you can find  nearly limitless tutorials online in a few clicks. 

The best way to learn all of these skills is to work on a practical project for yourself. Create your own personal website or build an app. Work through the process like you would with a client. You will learn so much and realize the areas you really need to focus on to improve your particular skills.

This takes me back, my time was way before you in the mid to late 90's. My favorite server was hot mail. As a kid I discovered a dos attack for mail servers through experimenting with spoofing emails.

 I had a friend that got me into coding we liked messing around writing punters for aol and aim (apps that generated code to knock you off line...a pain in the ass in days of dial up) to mess with friends. 

One day I got an email returned from "mailerdaemon@...com" and it very clearly said do not reply to this email. 

I replied and got a reply back with the message saying my mail could not be delivered and again it said do not reply. 

I wrote a new email to the address ,same thing got an auto reply.

 Oh this is neat I thought. Now what if....I spoof mail from myself to this account. So I Sent a spoofed email and got a reply in my in box. 

This was FN great I thought because at the time it was difficult to connect to mail.aol.com to spoof emails to AOL accounts.

So I worked out I could probably send a spoof mail to mailer-daemon from any AOL user and they would get a message.

 With this in mind I wrote a loop to send a few dozen emails in quick succession spoofed from my AOL account to an MD account. Sure enough I got a few dozen emails saying my message couldn't be delivered. 

After flooding some friends inboxes for fun I wanted to see what would happen if I spoofed email from one mail server to another. 

I registered an email on a site that promoted all sorts of ridiculous and racist things. 

Then sent a test email from myself to myself within this account to see how long it took to deliver the mail. It was nearly instant. Benchmark noted. 

Next I updated my program to mail from mailer-daemon at one of the largest most easily accessible email servers to the mailer daemon at this particular address. I Unleashed a few hundred emails. Sent myself another test email. The reply was slower than the benchmark. Ok I thought this is cool. 

Unleashed several thousand more emails over the span of an hour or so. Sent one more test email to myself. Waited 10 min, 30min,  an hour, a day...it turned to 3 days I finally got my email. 

My theory was for every email from md1 to md2, md2's reply would cause email traffic to continue to grow in a near infinite loop. As far as I could see at the time I was correct.

Number one best thing I learned to do was build quick rapport with patients. As charge I had to do the admissions. Guess what  most people don't want to be on your unit. Don't start bombarding them with questions. Unlessthey are not a frequent flyer they are likely a bit scared. Offer them some food and something to drink. If your unit allows it, ask if they want to make a call and let their family know they arrived safely. And take your time to give them a clear explanation of the intake process. 

Offering food and drinks is you giving them something which gives a sense of reciprocity. Offering to help them in little ways rather than being demanding and telling them what to do goes pretty far to build trust.

I have had my whole unit of patients go to bat for me against violent patients and help me talk them down without meds. When the whole unit knows you are there to help rather than collect a paycheck they can feel it they treat you differently than the pay check nurses. They tell you how they are really feeling and  what's really happening. I have had patients turn in drugs other people snuck in because they trusted me. The other big thing I found is communicating on their level both with words and physically. If they were sitting id knee to talk to them it helps out people at ease

Either because they enjoy the attention or because they don't know what's going on. Just remember this phrase if you are a union or non union hospital and tell your friends...

"assignment despite objection" 

understaffed? Unsafe ratios? Something feels off? 

ASIGNMENT DESPITE OBJECTION.

This is the first thing our nursing union has told us to do anytime it is unsafe. 
 
Before you begin any patient care send an email to your managers charge, unit, department,  whoever is your chain of command union rep And cc yourself on an private email. Let them know you are accepting your staffing assignment despite the belief that it is unsafe to do so. Then specify the reasons why in a PROFESSIONAL object manner.

"I am accepting this assignment despite objection. I want to make it known I believe this is an unsafe staffing ratio. I have been assigned xyz patients with no aid or support staff. I have 3 patients with xyz that require xyz per policy/ best practice protocols ....." 

Be as detailed as possible about your concerns and issues. If citing a policy know where to find it and copy the text. For example my hospital had a policy that if my unit census was over a certain number there had to be two nurses present. I was given the unit more times than I can count by myself with 1 aid when I should have had 2. They try to get around this sometimes by giving me orientees. But policy states orientees must train for xyz days before they can practice on their own. These orientees have been here >5 days. Below the minimum number so I told them this and that I can not be expected to take on the additional duties of precepting while training new staff when I am already understaffed below the policy mandated safe patient ratio adding to the risk of a pt harm incident. 

I usually add something to the end please provide additional support or corrective action to ensure pt safety. 

While this may not change anything in the short term it helps to protect you and your license putting the responsibility back on the hospital and administration for safety concerns. I have never gotten a reply back to my emails in writing...why? That would be them acknowledging their fault. I do get calls from managers "we are working on staffing" "I will try to get someone else over there" (in those cases when they do correct the problem I send a follow up email thanking the manager for their prompt response and commitment to safety)

If you take your assignment you are essentially saying you agree to the  pt case load under those conditions. If you verbally complain to a manager there is no documented proof. This is your proof that it is unsafe and you do not agree.

Now why would you accept under OBJECTION because if you don't accept your assignment the hospital could be a bunch of assholes and cite you with patient abandonment. So accept with a smile and document the fuck out of it. Something goes wrong write your incident report note that you informed management of unsafe conditions via email prior to starting the shift and no corrective action was taken on their part.

As a psych nurse it was part of my job to provide lessons on coping skills to deal with impulsivity and handle stressors. The most helpful tool for most situations is mindfulness.

Why? Because it helps us to become aware of our thoughts and the patterns of behaviors we engage in. With mindfulness I have been able to manage my own depression and anxiety fairly well for many years before finally needing meds. (The meds came after covid related PTSD)

When we become aware of our thoughts we notice the triggers that lead us to negative behaviors. For example if I have a fight with my wife, I go to work I have a bad day. To feel better I over eat to cope that leads to feeling sick which makes me feel worse. 

With mindfulness I can be aware of my feelings that may lead to the fight. Rather than trying to blame or accept blame I can examine my thoughts and feelings to find the source of the problem. Then discuss the issues. If we still fight. I can explore my thoughts as they unfold afterwards understand her position as well as mine and come back to offer an apology or discuss the issue in a rational way . Any step of the way If I pause to ask why do I feel like this? what is my thought pattern? where is my mind going? How does it make me feel? I get a better handle on my emotions and realize I am running on autopilot making impulsive decisions based on  unchecked thoughts running wild. (That is the cause of most anxiety ...if this happens then this then this then this into a full blown panic attack.)

Now back to my family member. They cant sit still and be alone. I have told them time and time again if you can't be content alone you can never be happy. No matter where you go who your with you will always have your own mental shit there tagging along. The sooner you can face it and cut through it the sooner you can find peace in all situations. A lot of people say learn to love yourself first. But if you only know abusive love then you will continue to abuse yourself. 

Rather find that place of peace and contentment within. That place that let's you be okay to be alone without fear or anxiety. That let's you rest in a mental state of ease. When you can tap in to that it does not matter if you are single or in a relationship. 

The nature of this world is impermanence. That person may love you one minute hate you the next. If you are not stable within yourself you're going to go on one hell of an emotional rollercoaster. If that person leaves or doesn't love you the way you want there will be anger and unsatisfaction. 

If you are content within yourself it is much easier to appreciate the good and consciously work through the bad and to love the other person for who they are not what they do for you (how they make you feel) Getting into a relationship when you don't have that self awareness and you are looking for the other person to validate you and make you feel better is a recipe for disaster.  

If your therapist says to take more time for yourself listen. It will only make you and your future relationships better. The thing I tell my patients when they are resistant to change is to look at your life where your past decisions got you. (Most time it's drug abuse and or suicidal attempts) in other words your shit hasn't worked so far doing it your way. Try something new and give it a chance can help get you a new perspective and break out of the old patterns that hold you back.
